clue.text: Just short of a maximum break, say something unrepeatable

definitions.text: Just short of a maximum break, say

blocks.clueFragment: Just short of a maximum break, say
blocks.note: first meaning: a single point below the top score, as a snooker break of 146 is to the 147 maximum
second meaning: a unique event that happens only once

explanation.surface: A snooker player falls agonisingly short of the perfect break and lets slip a remark that should never be repeated.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker the maximum break is 147; a player stuck on 146 is a single point off it.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the hyphenated phrase means a unique event or item that will not happen or be made again.

clue.text: Soporific work in theatre I took in

blocks.note: an operation is the work done in an operating theatre, shortened to op
taken as written
to take in food is to eat it, past tense

explanation.surface: A dull play sends the narrator to sleep at the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' suggests the stage, but here it is the surgeon's operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug derived from the poppy dulls the senses and induces sleep, so it is a sleep-inducing substance.

clue.text: Growth of intoxication with British coming aboard

indicators.note: something coming aboard gets inside a vessel, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: euphoria is the elated high of being intoxicated
B is the standard abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A drunken Briton staggers on board, flushed with drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growth' is used in the gardener's sense of a plant: the spurge family, whose members often have milky sap.
explanation.definitionFit: The spurges are a genus of plants, and a plant is a growing thing, hence a growth.

clue.text: Game with lover — stay drunk and party around pad

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so these letters lurch out of order

blocks.note: a fan is a devotee or lover of something
the letters of stay rearranged
an animal's pad is its foot
a ball is a formal dancing party

explanation.surface: A lover is urged to stay on, get drunk and party at someone's flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pad' looks like a flat, as in the surface, but it is a paw. 'Around' loosely places the party in the vicinity of the pad, i.e. next to it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a competition in which players pick imaginary squads of real players and score points from their performances, so it is a game.

clue.text: Beginning to buckle, woozily sedated — this should hold you up

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
woozy means dizzy and muddled, so the letters are jumbled up

blocks.note: the opening letter of buckle
the letters of sedated rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is sedated and starts to buckle at the knees, needing support.
explanation.walkthrough: After a sedative you would collapse onto just this; the definition reads the whole scene.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the frame of a bed, which supports the sleeper's weight above the floor.

clue.text: Yankee parking Sierra — European knocked over notice

indicators.note: something knocked over ends up upside down, which in a down entry turns the string around

blocks.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
Sierra is S in the NATO phonetic alphabet
E is the standard abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: An American parks his Spanish car and knocks over a European pedestrian.
explanation.walkthrough: Seat makes a car called the Sierra-sounding models, but here Sierra is only the radio code letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot or catch sight of something is to notice it, a slightly literary verb.

clue.text: Advertising, say, ‘Fashionable woolly, sturdy with navy top’?

indicators.note: woolly means fuzzy and confused, so these letters are muddled

blocks.note: the Royal Navy is known as the Senior Service
what is fashionable is in
the letters of sturdy rearranged

explanation.surface: An advertising slogan for a stylish, hard-wearing jumper with a navy-blue top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woolly' and 'navy top' dress the surface as clothing; a woolly is British for a knitted jumper. 'Top' puts the navy piece at the top of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Advertising sells a service rather than goods, so it is one example of this business sector, as the word 'say' admits.

clue.text: Join board

blocks.note: first meaning: to become a member of or sign up for, as with a competition
second meaning: to go into a ship, train or plane

explanation.walkthrough: 'Join board' reads like becoming a company director, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both signing up for something and going into a vehicle or building.

clue.text: Mathematician’s ring spanner

blocks.note: surface reading: a mechanic's closed wrench for gripping nuts
setter's reading: for a geometer, the straight line that spans a circle through its centre

explanation.surface: A mathematician turns out to own a set of mechanic's tools.
explanation.walkthrough: A ring spanner is a British name for a closed-end wrench; read literally it is whatever spans a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The straight line through the centre of a circle from edge to edge literally crosses the whole ring.

clue.text: Approach little troublemaker, getting wind up

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous child or small demon
to wind up something is to bring it to a close

explanation.surface: You go up to a naughty child who is getting worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind up' suggests teasing or reversal, but it simply means finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Something about to happen draws near or looms, so the verb means to come closer in time.

clue.text: Choose to eat before ‘Cheers’ that’s staged in theatre

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so one piece swallows another

blocks.note: to opt is to choose
ere is an old word for before
ta is British informal thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: Deciding to have dinner before a toast at a theatre show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' is British slang for thank you as well as a toast; here it means thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A light comic opera is a work performed on stage, so it is something put on in a theatre.

clue.text: To keep new, ‘create anew’ or ‘create again‘?

indicators.note: making something anew means forming it afresh, so the letters are rebuilt
to keep something is to hold it inside

blocks.note: the first of the two quoted uses of the word, taken as written
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A puzzle over wording: to keep something new, do you create it anew or create it again?
explanation.walkthrough: The word create is rearranged and N is placed in its middle. The quoted phrases look like alternative definitions, but only the second is.
explanation.definitionFit: To act out or bring into being once more is to repeat an earlier performance or enactment.

clue.text: Penny is so treacherous

blocks.note: first meaning: a coin bears a head on one side and a tail on the other
second meaning: deceitful, saying one thing and doing another

explanation.surface: A woman named Penny is accused of being a traitor.
explanation.walkthrough: Penny looks like a woman's name; it is the coin, which has heads and tails.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypocrite shows one face to you and another behind your back, so the term means deceitful.

clue.text: Something sticking out next to seaside church causes puncture

blocks.clueFragment: Something sticking out next to seaside
blocks.note: a pier is a structure jutting out into the sea from a resort
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A spike jutting out by a seaside church gives a cyclist a flat tyre.
explanation.walkthrough: Seaside piers, with amusements on them, are a feature of British resorts.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a hole through something with a point is to perforate or stab it, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Street remains cut off at the crest — it looks a little hairy

indicators.note: the crest is the top, so cutting there loses the first letter of a down entry

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street
rubble is the broken remains of a building

explanation.surface: A street of ruins on a hilltop looks a bit dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little hairy' suggests scary, but it means literally short hairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A short growth of beard after a day without shaving gives a slightly bristly look to the chin.

clue.text: Obnoxious friend interrupting over you once

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something

blocks.note: over in the sense of past or further than
thee is the old form of you
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A rude friend keeps butting in over the top of what you are saying.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pale was the English-ruled area around Dublin; anything outside it was thought uncivilised.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes behaviour so outrageous that it is unacceptable, offensive and objectionable.

clue.text: Plant Italy sited north of dam needs painting over?

blocks.note: painting is a form of art
I is the international vehicle code for Italy
to dam a flow is to block or choke it

explanation.surface: An Italian factory built upstream of a dam needs repainting.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'north of' and 'over' put the piece above: ART at the top, then I, then CHOKE.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe and Jerusalem kinds are thistle-like vegetables grown in gardens, so this is a plant.

clue.text: Climbing frame used by playmate’s pal I erected

indicators.note: the answer is used by the words that follow, sitting within them

blocks.note: runs from the end of playmate's into the start of erected

explanation.surface: A child's friend has put up a climbing frame in the playground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erected' in a down clue tempts a reversal, but the letters read straight down.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a lattice or trellis on which fruit trees and shrubs are trained to grow flat against a wall.

clue.text: Some MPs had to be in broadcast, with nice tab for travelling

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it
things that are travelling move about, so these letters shift

blocks.note: to sow seed is to broadcast it by scattering
taken as written
the letters of nice tab rearranged

explanation.surface: Politicians had to appear on air, and a generous expense account covered their journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' looks like radio or television, but it is the farmer's scattering of seed. In Britain the opposition's team of spokespeople mirroring government ministers has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposition frontbench politicians are a subset of Members of Parliament, hence some of them.

clue.text: ‘Respect‘ group that could lead Teesside announced twice

indicators.note: announced means spoken aloud, and twice tells us to hear both the place name and the team

blocks.note: Teesside spoken is 'T's side', a T team; the S team could precede it, as S comes before T

explanation.surface: A band or sports team that might top the bill in Teesside wins respect.
explanation.walkthrough: Teesside, around Middlesbrough in north-east England, is heard as 'T's side'. The side that could lead it alphabetically is the S team, which said aloud is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold someone in high regard is to admire them, so the noun and verb match.

clue.text: Swears when not given right money?

indicators.note: not given means withheld, so one letter standing for right is dropped

blocks.note: to swear something is to declare it firmly
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone curses because they were not paid the right amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swears' looks like cursing, but it is declaring on oath.
explanation.definitionFit: The resources a person or business owns, including cash and property, are their wealth, hence money.

clue.text: Mole I caught burrowing in, having capers?

indicators.note: burrowing in means digging into something and ending up inside it

blocks.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation
taken as written
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A mole digging around in the garden is caught frolicking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' looks like the burrowing animal, and 'burrowing' feeds that; it is a secret agent. Capers can be pickled buds, which add flavour, or risqué antics.
explanation.definitionFit: Food with pickled flower buds in it is piquant, and a racy story full of escapades is lively too.

clue.text: Storms following pound hitting lower amounts

blocks.note: f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
L is the symbol for pound sterling, from Latin libra
ounces are smaller weights than pounds

explanation.surface: Weather storms follow a fall in the pound against smaller currencies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storms' looks like weather but is a verb; an ounce is a sixteenth of a pound weight.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomp off in a temper with exaggerated movements is to flounce, as one storms out of a room.

clue.text: Four coming from Motown, 5 turned up

definitions.note: the answer completes the group name rather than replacing the phrase

indicators.note: turned up in a down entry means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: 5 down means notice, and to notice is to spot

explanation.surface: Four people from Detroit's record label spotted turning up.
explanation.walkthrough: The Four Tops were a Motown vocal group, so the answer is the word that follows 'Four'. The cross-reference points at the answer to 5 down, read as its synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The Detroit soul quartet were named the Four Tops, so the second word of their name is what goes with Four.

clue.text: Flipping parrot, a timid scoffing copycat

indicators.note: scoffing means gobbling down, so the words swallow the letters needed
flipping something over turns it back to front

blocks.note: the letters from the end of parrot through a to the start of timid

explanation.surface: A furious parrot, a shy one that wolfs down food and mimics everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parrot' is a tempting definition for a mimic, but it is just hiding the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who copies the behaviour or work of another is a mimic, which is what a copycat does.

clue.text: In safe?

blocks.note: first meaning: indoors in your own house rather than out
second meaning: comfortable and at ease, or in baseball a runner who has reached the final base

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the two words suggest something locked in a strongbox; they are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in one's own house means being indoors, and it also implies feeling secure and relaxed.

clue.text: Fan of Charles I might represent so artily

indicators.note: to represent is to present again in a different form, so the letters are recast

blocks.note: the letters of so artily rearranged

explanation.surface: A fan of King Charles might paint him in a rather artistic way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker, but it belongs to the king's name: Charles I, whose supporters fought the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters of the king against Parliament in the 1640s were called Cavaliers, and generally a supporter of monarchy.

clue.text: Solved my clue? It’s old but could be enlightening

definitions.text: It’s old but could be enlightening

indicators.note: a solved puzzle has had its pieces worked out and put in a new order

blocks.note: the letters of my clue rearranged

explanation.surface: A solver finishes the clue and hopes an old puzzle will prove illuminating.
explanation.walkthrough: The original was the school where Aristotle taught in ancient Athens, an old place of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle's ancient Athenian school, and later lecture halls named after it, existed to educate, hence old and enlightening.
